data.gender_notes: Uditi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Uditi is a unisex name derived from the Sanskrit word 'udita', meaning 'risen' or 'ascending'. The name Uditi carries the meaning “Rising, Ascending” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Uditi usually hope their child will grow to embody rising, ascending and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Uditi was a renowned Jain scholar and monk who lived during the 12th to 13th centuries CE. He is known for his works on Jain logic and metaphysics, particularly his commentary on the Nyayasutras called the 'Uddyotana'.

Another reference to Uditi comes from the Jain text, 'Harivamsha-purana', where he is mentioned as a noble donor and patron of Jain monks. Uditi is also described as a king who ruled over the region known as Magadha during the 5th century BCE.
